chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
He was asked about touching the Kaaba, so he said: 'From its back.'

key_terms.اسْتِلَامُ: Touching or kissing the Kaaba as a ritual act
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Kaaba, the cubic building in Mecca
key_terms.دُبُرِهَا: Its back (the side opposite the door)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to touch the Kaaba from its back side during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the ritual of *Istilam* (touching or kissing the Kaaba) is not strictly limited to the corners or the door, but can be performed from the back of the structure. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the physical orientation of the pilgrim, emphasizing the spiritual intent of connection with the House of God over rigid positional constraints. The back of the Kaaba, known as *Al-Multazam*, is thus recognized as a valid locus for this act of devotion.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having been asked about touching the Kaaba. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the back of it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about touching al-Ka‘bah.
He (the Imam) said, ‘You should touch its backside.’”
